title: IPO Report Card: 30 to 60 Days After Listing — August 2026
description: Out of 28 IPOs that listed between 30 and 60 days ago, 18 are currently trading above their original issue price. 10 companies are trading below their IPO pri.

faq.a: SME IPOs are Initial Public Offerings by Small and Medium Enterprises, which list on dedicated platforms like NSE Emerge or BSE SME, typically for smaller companies with different listing requirements than Mainboard IPOs.

Mainboard IPOs are for larger companies that list on the main stock exchanges (National Stock Exchange and Bombay Stock Exchange), generally requiring higher market capitalisation and meeting more stringent regulations.

faq.q: What does 'return vs. issue price' mean?
faq.a: This figure shows the percentage change between the original IPO price and the current market price, indicating the profit or loss an investor would have if they were allotted shares in the IPO and held them until today.

faq.q: Can an IPO price go below its issue price?
faq.a: Yes, absolutely. If market demand is not strong enough, or if investors perceive the company's valuation as too high, the share price can fall below its original IPO price after listing.

faq.q: What is the purpose of an IPO?
faq.a: Companies issue IPOs primarily to raise capital (money) from the public to fund business expansion, reduce debt, or for other corporate purposes, and also to provide liquidity for existing shareholders to sell their shares.
